title: Fungi
subtitle: Threads in the dark
summary: A mushroom is only the fruit. The fungus itself is a net of threads in soil and wood, eating from the outside, and it runs much of the living world: it rots the forest floor, feeds the roots of trees, farms algae as lichens, glows in the dark and makes antibiotics. Each lesson opens on a real puzzle, a ring in a meadow, a spoiled plate in Fleming's lab, a fossil trunk eight metres tall, and follows the evidence, with live figures you can push. Not a guide to eating anything.
